title: Source shift gauge for flat telescope normalization
statement: Let f: Z → Y be proper between Noetherian schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], with derived categories in a common localization universe [def-pc-derived-category], F = derivedPullback f [def-pc-derived-pullback], a supplied strong monoidal structure [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], and additive termwise tensor pullback H [def-pc-module-pullback]. Put Q = Qh_Y and G = H followed by Qh_Z. Fix a counit ε: Q⋙F → G making F a left derived functor, and a coherent integer shift on F for which ε commutes with shifts. There exist e: F(O_Y[1]) ≅ O_Z[1] and a natural automorphism a of Q⋙F such that, for each concrete flat telescope P [def-sc-flat-telescope-stage-map] and X=q(P), a_(X[1]);commShift_(Q⋙F)(X) = F(commShift_Q(X));b(Q(X));a_X[1], where b(K)=F(c_Y(K) inverse);δ_F(O_Y[1],K);(e tensor id);c_Z(F(K)), and c is the canonical shift-unit comparison [def-sc-scheme-canonical-shift-unit-iso]. The assertion is only about the shift gauge on the source functor; no comparison with G, invertibility of ε components, or extension of the equation beyond telescopes is part of its conclusion.

proof.text: Compute the canonical shift comparison using bounded-above flat stages, their countable sum, and the cone of one minus transition. Use degree-zero and translated unit models.

Normalize the unit by the supplied monoidal unit map. Rewrite translation as tensor with the translated unit by the Koszul comparison and the translated left unitor. Apply the supplied inverse tensorator. Its two unit equations identify the unit normalizations, and its associativity equation identifies the tensor rewrites on the two summands of the transition cone. Take the ratio with the original representative comparison.

The model ratios commute with the sum inclusions and transition maps, hence the cone differential. Compare K-flat resolutions and apply the right Kan universal property of the supplied counit to descend the ratio and its reverse to inverse natural transformations on Qh followed by derived pullback. The equation on each telescope is the displayed shift gauge equation.
